blocks.s: This page is shown on the Tools dashboard (Developments → How a tool is built). It is written in plain language for Harry; the exact rules and API are in `CLAUDE.md`. If this page and the code disagree, the code is right: fix this page.

A tool is one file that says what questions to make. Everything else (the three modes, the buttons, printing, links, the pictures that build up) is done by a shared shell, so the tool file only holds the maths.

items: You (or a spec in `specs/`) say what the tool should teach.
The tool file turns that into questions and worked answers.
One line in `src/registry.ts` puts it on the site. Nothing else needs editing to add a route or a landing-page card.
The shell (`src/shared/ToolShell.tsx`) wraps the tool and gives it Whiteboard, Worked Example, Worksheet, printing, share links and the rest.
Tests check every tool automatically.
A script reads the code and writes the facts the dashboard shows. You never type those.

guide.title: What is inside a tool file

blocks.s: A tool lives in `src/tools/<Strand>/<Name>.tsx`. In order, a tool file holds:

head: Part
What it is
Be aware
rows: Types
The small shapes the tool uses for its own numbers
Local to the file. Do not redefine shared types
`TOOL_CONFIG`
The tabs (sub-tools), the levels, and the Question Options (the switches a teacher can tick)
Options that are alternatives belong in one pool; switches that can stack are separate. See "Question Options" in `CLAUDE.md`
`INFO_SECTIONS`
The text in the (i) information box
Comes from the spec's info section
`generateQuestion`
Makes one question: the display, the answer and the worked steps
Must give every question a `key` that describes it (never just a random number) so a worksheet does not repeat
`export const __test`
Hands the config and generator to the automatic tests
Never delete it. The build fails if a shell tool lacks it
`export default function App()`
Renders `<ToolShell … />`
Leave as the template has it

blocks.s: Sample questions in the spec (the "acceptance reference") are the definition of correct: check your tool produces those shapes and answers.

guide.title: What the shell does for you (do not rebuild it)

blocks.s: Whiteboard, Worked Example (step by step, with the line building up one mark at a time), Worksheet (columns, differentiated levels, fullscreen), PDF printing, the level buttons, Question Options popovers, the colour picker, the (i) box, share links, recent and pinned questions, the ink pen on every page, and Teach / Lessons / Depth when a tool supplies them. A tool never writes its own buttons, popovers, print window or link handling.

head: File or folder
What it is for
Be aware
rows: `src/registry.ts`
The one list of every tool: id, path, name, description, strand, whether it is live
`enabled: false` means in development (only shows with Developing tools on). Never edit `App.tsx` or the landing page to add a tool
`src/shared/ToolShell.tsx`
The shell for question generators
About 2,100 lines in one component; change with care (see the decision tree)
`src/shared/index.ts`
The barrel: the one door tools import through
Tools import from `../../shared` only. Several tools still reach around it (a recorded decision)
`src/shared/types.ts`
Shared shapes: questions, steps, config, options
Underscore fields on a question (`_diagram`, `_rawValues`…) are the private hand-over between tool and shell and are not type-checked
`src/shared/helpers.ts`
Everyday generator helpers: `randInt`, `pick`, `step`, `mStep`, `tStep`, `fracStr`, `pickActive`, `fmt`
`mStep` is the default way to write a working step. Never put `\text{}` inside a step
`src/shared/math.ts`
Shared number maths: `gcd`, `lcm`, `gcdAll`, `shuffle`
`gcd` is never negative; `lcm` is 0 if either number is 0; `shuffle` is fair and returns a new list. Use these, do not write local copies. More helpers are listed as decisions
`src/shared/prompts.ts`
Says a shared prompt ("Simplify:") once on a worksheet
A question shaped as a maths-free line then a maths-only line gets this for free
`src/shared/print.ts`, `printDiagram.ts`, `worksheetLayout.ts`
Printing: text sheets, picture sheets, and the page-fill engine both share
Picture tools pass `handleDiagramPrint` and never hand-roll a print grid
`src/shared/layoutMode.ts`
Decides phone, tablet or laptop layout, including the "View as" override
Never read `matchMedia` yourself; use `useLayoutMode()`
`src/shared/placeValue.ts`, `ratioTable.ts`, `counters.ts`, `sigFigs.ts`, `carry.ts`, `longDivision.ts`
The pictures (representations) and their data
Pick one of the eight core pictures before inventing a new one
`src/shared/components/`
The shared screens and widgets (question display, popovers, tables, Depth stage, ink pen)
Tools use these through the barrel
`src/shared/depth.ts`, `lessons.ts`, `TeachingDeck.tsx`
Depth questions, lessons, and Teach slide decks
Optional extras a tool opts into
`src/shared/calibration.ts`
Measures how hard questions are so worksheets run easy to hard
Re-run the calibration after any change to a calibrated generator
`src/shared/decision/`, `src/shared/cs/`
The two other shells (Decision Maths; Computer Science revision)
Separate by design; they do not use `ToolShell`
`src/tests/`
The automatic checks
`generators.test.ts` renders every maths string for every tool; `organisation.test.ts` fails if a tool is unregistered or uncategorised
`src/generated/toolFacts.json`
The facts the dashboard shows, read from the code
Never edit by hand. Run `npm run facts` after changing a tool or the registry, and commit the result
`src/admin/`
The dashboard itself
Reads the generated facts and the notes
`api/`
The small server piece that stores the dashboard notes
Cannot import from `src/`
`specs/`
Briefs: what to build, with the sample answers that define correct
Only briefs marked `Status: ready` are built; mark `implemented` when done
`scripts/`
`new-tool` (scaffolds a tool), `toolFacts` (the facts), `notesPages` (planner pages), `adminDocs` (these dashboard pages)
Run through `npm run …`
`docs/`
The written project: plan, tidy-up list, history, glossary, design notes
See the documentation map in `CLAUDE.md`
`CLAUDE.md`
The rules Claude reads every session
The single source of truth for conventions

guide.title: Extra files that sit beside a tool

blocks.s: A bigger tool can have helper files next to it, named after it:

items: `<Tool>Depth.ts` holds the Depth questions (for example `OrderOfOperationsDepth.ts`).
`<Tool>Lessons.ts` holds the lesson steps; `<Tool>Teach.ts` holds the Teach slides.
`<Tool>.calibration.ts` holds the measured difficulty table. It is written by a test run, not by hand.
Large tools split their maths into `…Core.ts`, `…Algebra.ts` and so on (Indices does this).

blocks.s: Each of these is optional and only appears when the tool passes it to the shell.

items: Import from `../../shared` only; never import another tool.
Never edit a generated file. Run `npm run facts` and commit the result; a test fails if it is stale.
Keep `__test`. Without it the tool is not checked.
Keys must describe the question so a worksheet does not repeat itself.
Check the three screen sizes (phone, tablet, laptop) by hand for anything with a custom picture.
Developing tools mode hides unfinished things (tools with `enabled: false`, Teach decks, lessons). A tool goes live by deleting `enabled: false`.
A worksheet generated from a calibrated tool is spread across measured difficulty; the Smart Progressor switch turns this off.
Work on a fresh branch, run `npm install` first, and make sure `npm run build` and `npm test` pass before pushing.

guide.title: Making a new tool, in order

blocks.s: 1. Have a brief in `specs/` (or answer the questions in `CLAUDE.md`). 2. `npm run new-tool -- --name "Display Name" --category <Folder> --path /url --description "One sentence."` copies the template and registers it as in development. 3. Fill in the types, `TOOL_CONFIG`, `INFO_SECTIONS` and `generateQuestion`; write worked steps with `mStep`. 4. Check the sample questions from the brief come out right. 5. `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm test`. 6. Run `npm run facts` and commit the JSON. 7. Remove `enabled: false` when it is ready to go live. 8. Update the tool's dashboard notes, the patch notes, and the planner Build Log.
